subject: Temporary carve matrix + autoscale override proposal for Solara Health pilot
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary carve matrix + autoscale override proposal for Solara Health pilot

Team —

Quick ask: Solara Health is starting a 3-week integration pilot (production-like traffic) on May 17 and they need a predictable headroom window to run end-to-end latency/regression sweeps and live A/B evaluation. They signed a short-term commitment and have regulatory requirements around inference availability.

What I'm proposing (attached: capacity_plan_v2.xlsx):
- Temporary carve: reserve a 16-GPU slab (8xA100 equivalent) for 3 weeks (May 17–June 7) scoped to Solara pilot only.
- Autoscale override window: allow soft autoscale limit increase to +30% for that slab during 08:00–20:00 PT weekdays to avoid cold-start throttles for batch sweeps. Outside that window, normal preemption applies.
- Fallback routing: route overflow to a cheaper quantized variant (q8b) with automatic degradation monitoring and rollback.

Operational constraints / asks:
1) Can Allocations/Provisioning carve out the slab without violating current QOS constraints for enterprise customers?
2) Can Ops implement the time-bounded autoscale override (signal-based, reversible) and add the quick rollback runbook?
3) Product: any objections to allowing the quantized fallback for Solara's eval runs (we'll instrument quality checks)?

I want to align before I confirm scope with their ops lead (Maya). If we can, I'll attach the MOU language and timeline.

Thanks —
Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Partnerships & Pilots
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0124

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary carve matrix + autoscale override proposal for Solara Health pilot

Steph —

Thanks for the succinct ask and the spreadsheet. High-level product take: the quantized fallback is acceptable for short-duration evals provided we gate it behind the quality monitoring hooks (prompt-based sampling we discussed) and an automated rollback if perplexity / specific metrics drop by > 8%. Please add the evaluation prompt-set to the Drive link.

Two product questions:
- Are the regression sweeps latency-sensitive or mostly throughput-driven? If latency-sensitive we should tighten the autoscale window to 10:00–18:00 PT.
- Do we expect sustained KV cache warmups? If yes, we need to increase the headroom to 20 GPUs so synthetic traffic doesn't evict other customers' hot caches.

I'll greenlight the fallback once we have the eval gating and the exact expected QPS during sweep windows.

-j

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Product, Dedicated
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary carve matrix + autoscale override proposal for Solara Health pilot

Looping in ops details / feasibility. I attached a short ops_runbook.pdf with the proposed signal and rollback steps. TL;DR: doable with the following caveats:

1) Current pool utilization: the candidate pool (us-west-2 dedicated pool B) is at 78% baseline for May; carving 16 GPUs will push effective utilization to ~87% on peak weekdays. That is above our soft threshold and increases eviction risk for lower-tier commitments.

2) Mitigations I recommend:
- Convert the carve to a "time-partitioned reserved slab": 08:00–20:00 PT dedicated to Solara; 20:00–08:00 PT released back to general pool. This preserves overnight batch capacity for other customers.
- Autoscale override should be implemented as a transient policy with automatic 1-hour cooldown and a manual approval channel for ops if the override triggers more than 3 times/day.
- Add a preemptible notification web-hook to Solara and an internal ticketing alert (Jira: SUP-6719) when fallback routing occurs.

3) If Product increases headroom to 20 GPUs (per Jonas' note) I need pre-approval from Capacity Governance (Marcus) because that crosses the tranche we promised to a legacy enterprise customer (Aurora Fin).

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm whether we can move 16->20 GPUs for a 3-week window and whether finance approvals are required? If not, we proceed with 16 and the time-partitioned slab.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Infrastructure PM, Dedicated Operations
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Maya Patel <maya@solarahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudPartner Ops <ops@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary carve matrix + autoscale override proposal for Solara Health pilot

Thanks, Stephanie / Kim —

Solara's ops team is comfortable with the proposed time-partitioned slab (08:00–20:00 PT). A couple of asks on our side:

- Could you confirm SLAs for the dedicated window (P99 tail latency goal)? We need a commitment for the pilot report.
- We prefer the autoscale override to be capped at +20% rather than +30% to limit variability in cost estimates.
- Please share the fallback quality gating criteria so our clinical reviewers can sign off.

We can accept 16 GPUs if we get the time-boxed guarantee and the gating thresholds. Attached is our pilot checklist (referenced, not attached here).

Best,
Maya

Maya Patel
Head of SRE, Solara Health
maya@solarahealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary carve matrix + autoscale override proposal for Solara Health pilot

Ok — I checked the tranche commitments and finance exposure. Quick summary and decision: 

- We can approve a 16-GPU time-partitioned reserved slab (08:00–20:00 PT) for May 17–June 7 with the autoscale override capped at +20% as Solara requested.
- We cannot increase to 20 GPUs without pushing an Aurora Fin mitigation plan; that would require a separate executive approval and a finance offset.
- Ops: proceed to implement the transient policy (Kim) and wire the Jira alert SUP-6719.
- Product: Jonas, please add the eval prompt-set and the automated rollback gating doc to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow so we can include it in the pilot MOU.

I'll log the carve in Capacity Governance and notify Aurora Fin with a heads-up note that we are taking a time-bounded slab.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Capacity Governance Lead
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
